themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Reports of door and window damage surged to 4 complaints THIS WEEK, a 540% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.6 per week (z-score: 3.94), signaling a potential concentrated incident or emerging building safety issue in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: 4 door/window complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing suggests concentrated incident or emerging pattern requiring investigation
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike: break-ins, weather damage, construction accident, or vandalism trend?
Which neighborhoods/blocks are affected and whether residents feel safe

themes_detail.label: Water System Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints nearly doubled THIS WEEK to 12 reports, a 153% spike over the 8-week baseline of 4.8 per week (z-score: 3.78), suggesting possible infrastructure stress or widespread service disruptions in the district.
evidence: 12 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Concentrated timing suggests acute infrastructure problem rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Is this a localized main break, pressure issue, or citywide problem affecting Lower Manhattan disproportionately?
Impact on residents: affected buildings, boil water advisories, or service outages

themes_detail.label: Standing Water Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints exploded to 3 reports LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike over the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69), indicating possible drainage failure, flooding, or waterproofing issues following recent weather.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Extreme baseline deviation suggests rare, acute event rather than seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Weather trigger: did recent heavy rain expose drainage infrastructure failures?
Which streets/areas are affected and whether mosquito control or flooding risk exists

themes_detail.label: Construction Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 30 reports LAST WEEK, a 329% increase over the 8-week baseline of 7.0 per week (z-score: 8.85), the highest-severity spike in the dataset, coinciding with 1,253 active DOB permits and suggesting coordinated renovation wave.
evidence: 30 construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Spike represents 329% increase (z-score: 8.85, severity: high—highest in dataset)
1,253 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days (1,078 alterations, 27 new buildings) indicate sustained building activity
reporting_angles: Coordination: are multiple major projects (101 Franklin, 65 Franklin developments, etc.) driving synchronized construction noise and disruption?
Resident impact: noise complaints, hours violations, traffic disruption from concurrent projects in Lower Manhattan

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining & Vendor Chaos
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints quadrupled to 5 reports LAST WEEK (400% spike, z-score: 4.0) and mobile food vendor complaints surged to 5 (344% spike, z-score: 4.18), both simultaneous spikes suggesting enforcement gaps or post-policy change confusion in street vending regulation.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% increase, z-score: 4.0)
5 mobile food vendor complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% increase, z-score: 4.18)
Dual spike timing suggests coordinated enforcement or new regulatory environment affecting street commerce
reporting_angles: Did new outdoor dining or vending rules trigger complaints, or are enforcement operations ramping up?
Small business impact: how are vendors and restaurateurs navigating permit/compliance requirements?
